tool_input.command:
mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/tls-verification.md <<'EOF'
# TLS certificate verification

TLS certificate verification is enabled on all builds, including development builds; there is no exception that disables it for local testing. This is consistent with the project's separate decision to enforce HTTPS everywhere, with no plaintext exception for any service.
EOF
cat docs/policies/tls-verification.md

result:
I created `docs/policies/tls-verification.md` with a one-paragraph statement. It says certificate verification is on for all builds, including development builds, with no exception for local testing. It also notes the related decision to enforce HTTPS everywhere with no plaintext exception for any service.

Both statements come from recorded decisions: #31 for verification on all builds, and #34 for HTTPS everywhere. The earlier plan to turn verification off in dev builds was replaced by #31, so I left it out.

The first attempt to write the file through Bash was rejected by the shell, so I used the Write tool instead. The file is in place, but I haven't read it back.
